title: Preparing Data for Visualization
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of Preparing Data for Visualization.
Apply Preparing Data for Visualization to a realistic Python data task.
Choose suitable Python structures and standard-library tools for the task.
Identify data-quality, correctness and interpretation risks.
Build a small reproducible analysis artifact using Preparing Data for Visualization.

understand.concept: A visualization should answer a specific question with an appropriate chart and clearly labeled units. Before plotting, aggregate data to the right level, choose meaningful categories, handle missing values and verify totals. A chart can mislead through truncated axes, inconsistent scales, overloaded categories or missing context.
understand.whyItMatters: Reliable analysis depends on transparent decisions about data meaning, quality and interpretation—not merely on producing a number or chart.
understand.analogy: A data analyst is like a careful investigator who checks the evidence, records each transformation and explains how a conclusion was reached.
understand.analogyLimit: Datasets are not always complete or representative, and a neat summary cannot remove bias or prove causation.
understand.summary: Preparing Data for Visualization provides a practical foundation for trustworthy Python data analysis.

explain.narrative: Prepare a small sequence of labels and values, sort categories deliberately, choose a chart type that matches the comparison and include a title, axis labels, units and source context. Bar charts compare categories; line charts show ordered trends; scatter plots show relationships between numeric variables. This lesson focuses on preparing trustworthy plotting data; Matplotlib installation and rendering are covered when the package-enabled runtime is available.

examples.title: Prepare labels and values
examples.code:
summary = {'North': 12, 'South': 9}
labels = list(summary.keys())
values = list(summary.values())
print(len(labels) == len(values))
examples.explanation: Each label must correspond to exactly one plotted value.

examples.title: Sort categories for a chart
examples.explanation: A deterministic category order improves comparison.

examples.title: Compute a baseline
examples.explanation: A baseline can help interpret values, but the chart should explain what it represents.

examples.title: Check equal lengths
examples.explanation: Mismatched labels and values can cause plotting errors or misleading mappings.

examples.title: Format a readable label
examples.explanation: Formatting adds readable units and thousands separators.

practise.guidedTask: Prepare a monthly sales summary with ordered month labels, numeric totals, a title, axis labels and currency units. Explain why a line chart is appropriate.
practise.independentTask: Choose one category comparison and one time trend from synthetic data. Decide which chart type fits each question and list the labels and units required.
hints: Match chart type to the question.
Avoid hiding zero or negative values unintentionally.
practise.challenge: Design a chart-ready summary function that validates equal label/value lengths, rejects non-finite values and returns a documented plotting specification.
validationCriteria: The data question and input assumptions are explicit.
All examples execute and match their expected output on Python 3.13.
Missing, invalid and boundary cases are handled deliberately.
The analysis preserves units and documents limitations.
The solution is reproducible and does not expose private data.

questions.prompt: Which chart is usually suitable for a time trend?
questions.explanation: A line chart communicates ordered change over time.

questions.prompt: What must align in a category chart?
questions.answer: Each label and its corresponding value
options: Each label and its corresponding value
The colors and font size only
questions.explanation: Misaligned labels and values produce incorrect interpretation.
Units tell readers what the numeric scale represents.

questions.prompt: What should be checked before plotting totals?
questions.answer: That plotted aggregates reconcile with source data
options: That plotted aggregates reconcile with source data
That every bar has a different color
That the chart has no title
questions.explanation: Reconciliation catches aggregation and filtering errors.

questions.prompt: Does a chart prove a causal relationship?
options: Yes, if it is a line chart
questions.explanation: Visual association is not causal evidence.
